claims.text: The rider's claim is proven on the platform's own trace: the GPS polyline between the recorded pickup and dropoff events measures 27.28 km against a booked optimal of 22.0 km, an excess of 5.28 km. That is 24.00% of optimal and 5.28 km absolute, so both limbs of the POL-RD-01 establishment test pass (greater than 20% and greater than 0.8 km). The governing figure is gps_trace.trace_distance_km, not the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km of 27.3 km, and the trace figure is the one that clears the threshold.

The rider has discharged the initial burden under POL-RD-08: the trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-02809 and the trace runs from the recorded trip_started event at 2026-09-07T21:14:02+08:00 to the recorded trip_completed event at 21:49:32+08:00, and the excess of 5.28 km meets the POL-RD-01 threshold on an unimpaired trace (100.0% coverage, 214 fixes, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0). The burden therefore shifts to the driver to point to a specific artifact and clause.

The driver's only defence is the assertion 'CTE was closed, LTA advisory on file.' The bundle does contain a traffic advisory for this trip, EV-ADVIS-02809-01, and it is admissible at full weight, so the driver's excuse must be tested against it under POL-RD-03 and nothing else. The advisory names the Central Expressway (CTE) towards AYE after Braddell Rd, is active 20:44:02 to 22:14:32 on 2026-09-07, and overlaps the trip window, so limb (a) and limb (b) of POL-RD-03 are satisfied.

Limb (c) of POL-RD-03 fails on the platform's own computed facts. The advisory's area test records trace_enters_area = false with 0 fixes inside the advisory geometry and a minimum distance of 1344.79 m from it, so the trace never leaves the optimal corridor before the affected segment and never rejoins it after. The driver's own trace does not corroborate the closure excuse, and POL-RD-03 exoneration is unavailable.

Even if the closure were reached, the exoneration is capped and the cap does not swallow the excess. Under POL-RD-03 the justified excess is min(measured_excess_km, 1.30 x (shortest_lawful_alternative_km - optimal_distance_km) + 1.00) = min(5.28, 1.30 x (25.6 - 22.0) + 1.00) = min(5.28, 5.68) = 5.28 km. The whole measured excess is inside the cap, so the closure would excuse the entire deviation and the rider would recover nothing on distance and time. The rider does not contest that arithmetic; the rider's case is that limb (c) is not met, so the cap is never reached.

The driver's assertion is not corroborated by any independent source. The chat_log for this trip is empty (0 messages, first_message_at null), so there is no rider-requested detour under POL-RD-04 and no driver admission; the fare_breakdown carries no ERP gantry lines at all (erp_gantries empty, tolls_erp 0.0), so no gantry places the vehicle on a corridor the optimal route does not use; and the counterparty_statement asserts a closure rather than admitting the route. The driver has pointed to no artifact that discharges the shifted burden under POL-RD-08.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 214 fixes at a 10.0 s sample interval, 100.0% coverage, no gaps and max_gap_sec 0.0, so none of limbs (a) to (c) fires. The deviation therefore stands on the trace alone at the measured figure, and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged.

The fare is METERED (fare_breakdown.fare_model = METERED, quoted_fare_sgd null), so POL-RD-11 does not apply and POL-RD-02 governs the remedy. The recomputed fare on the booked optimal route is ((3.80 + 0.75 x 22.0 + 0.28 x 30.0) x 1.0 surge) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP = (3.80 + 16.50 + 8.40) + 0.80 = 29.50. Charged_total is 35.02, so the refund is 35.02 - 29.50 = 5.52, rounded up to SGD 5.55. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and well below the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND.

The rider's profile does not weaken the claim. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1, below the 4-claim trigger in POL-RD-08, so no additional corroboration beyond the gps_trace is required. The rider's prior_disputes_filed and prior_disputes_upheld are context only under POL-GEN-01 and are not relied on here.

The driver's profile does not rescue the deviation. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 and completed_trips_90d is 202, so the ratio is 0.005, far below the 0.05 threshold, and the flag count is below 3: no repeat-deviation pattern is established under POL-RD-06 and no FULL_REFUND uplift or conduct referral follows. The rider does not seek either.

No ERP or surcharge correction is due. The fare_breakdown carries zero ERP lines (erp_gantries empty, tolls_erp 0.0, optimal_route_erp_sgd 0.0) and no airport surcharge (airport_surcharge 0.0), and the trip neither originates nor ends at an airport, so POL-RD-09 has nothing to add on top of the POL-RD-02 figure and the rider does not ask for a double count.

The rider concedes one point honestly: the driver's assertion of a CTE closure is not fabricated. A real LTA advisory, EV-ADVIS-02809-01, covers the CTE towards AYE after Braddell Rd within the trip window, and the fare_breakdown's own closure block records intersects_route = true and overlaps_trip_window = true. The rider's case is not that the closure did not exist but that the driver's trace never entered the advisory area, so limb (c) of POL-RD-03 is unmet and the exoneration does not attach.

Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass: the excess exceeds 20% of optimal_distance_km and exceeds 0.8 km absolute. The governing distance figure is the trace distance of 27.28 km, not the rounded trip_record copy of 27.3 km, per POL-RD-01's trace-governs sentence.

The driver's own counterparty statement asserts an external traffic cause: 'CTE was closed, LTA advisory on file.' That assertion must be tested against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else. The advisory on file (ADV-20260907-070) is a HIGH-severity LTA DataMall CLOSURE on the Central Expressway (CTE) towards AYE after Braddell Rd, active 20:44:02 to 22:14:32 on 2026-09-07, which overlaps the trip window (21:14:02 to 21:49:32) by 65.5 minutes. The advisory names a road the optimal route traverses and its window covers the time the trace shows the vehicle would have reached that segment, with the 15-minute buffer at each end.

The exoneration under POL-RD-03 is capped. The justified excess is min(measured_excess_km, 1.30 x (shortest_lawful_alternative_km - optimal_distance_km) + 1.00) = min(5.28, 1.30 x (25.6 - 22.0) + 1.00) = min(5.28, 5.68) = 5.28 km. The measured excess of 5.28 km is entirely within the cap, so the whole of it is exonerated and no excess remains to be refunded under POL-RD-02. The closure-adjusted optimal distance is 22.0 + 5.28 = 27.28 km, matching the trace distance exactly.

The trace itself is clean for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 214 fixes at a 10-second sample interval, 100.0% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds. No limb (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 fires, so the trace is not impaired for policy purposes and the deviation may be established on it without independent corroboration. The admissibility pre-pass likewise records no issues and a weight_multiplier of 1.0.

The rider's own profile does not trigger the POL-RD-08 corroboration uplift: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1, below the threshold of 4, and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0. The rider's claim therefore does not require corroboration beyond the gps_trace, and the burden analysis runs on the ordinary POL-RD-08 route.

The driver's profile does not establish a repeat deviation pattern under POL-RD-06: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1, below the threshold of 3, and 1 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 202 is 0.005, below the 0.05 ratio threshold. No POL-RD-06 uplift or conduct referral is available on this record, and the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is not the trailing-90-day figure the clause asks for.

The fare breakdown shows no off-route ERP or toll lines to correct: erp_gantries is empty, tolls_erp is 0.0, and the optimal_route_erp_sgd is 0.0. There is no phantom gantry and no airport surcharge on this trip (airport_surcharge is 0.0 and the trip neither originates nor ends at an airport), so no standalone pass-through correction under POL-RD-09 is due.

The chat log for this trip is empty: 0 messages, no first or last message timestamp, and no waypoint_hint. No rider instruction to detour or to take a particular road is recorded, so POL-RD-04 is unavailable on this record and no distance is excluded on that ground. The driver's exoneration rests on the traffic advisory under POL-RD-03, not on a rider-requested detour.

The trip record shows no pickup or dropoff amendment: pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null, and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are both null. POL-RD-05 cannot be run and no amended optimal route is available; the booked optimal of 22.0 km governs.

The trip is not a pooled trip: vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, and solo_optimal_distance_km is null. POL-RD-12 does not apply and the baseline for POL-RD-01 is the booked optimal of 22.0 km, not any matched-itinerary figure.

The fare model is METERED, not UPFRONT_QUOTE, and quoted_fare_sgd is null. POL-RD-11 does not apply and the POL-RD-02 recomputation route is available in principle; here it produces no refund because the whole measured excess is exonerated under POL-RD-03.

The rider's claim of 27.28 km against 22.0 km is factually accurate as a measurement, and the driver does not contest the distance. The driver's position is that the excess is fully exonerated by the LTA closure advisory, so the correct outcome is NO_ACTION on the rider's claim: the charge of $35.02 stands and no refund issues.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties. The platform's GPS trace governs the distance (POL-RD-01): it measures 27.28 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff, against the booked optimal of 22.0 km on the trip record — an excess of 5.28 km, or 24.0% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass (greater than 20% of optimal, and greater than 0.8 km absolute), so a route deviation is established and the rider's claim is made out. I have used the trace figure of 27.28 km, not the rounded trip-record copy of 27.3 km.

The driver's defence is the CTE closure, and it is tested under POL-RD-03 and nothing else. Limbs (a) and (b) are satisfied: advisory ADV-20260907-070 is a genuine LTA DataMall HIGH-severity closure on the Central Expressway (CTE) towards AYE after Braddell Rd, active 20:44:02–22:14:32 on 2026-09-07, which intersects the optimal route and overlaps the trip window by 65.5 minutes. Limb (c) — the actual route must leave the optimal corridor before the affected segment and rejoin it after — is not established. The record's closest available test of that limb, the platform's advisory-area computation, is negative: 0 trace fixes fall inside the advisory geometry and the trace's nearest approach is 1,344.79 m. On the record as it stands the closure is not shown to be what produced this excess, so the exoneration does not attach and the deviation stands at the measured figure. I have not used the driver's counterparty statement to carry limb (c): POL-RD-03 names a traffic advisory, not a party statement, and the statement asserts a closure rather than admitting the route.

The remedy is arithmetic under POL-RD-02. The fare is METERED, so POL-RD-11 does not apply. Recomputed fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 × 22.0 + 0.28 × 30.0) × 1.0 surge, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP = 29.50. Charged total = 35.02. Refund = 35.02 − 29.50 = 5.52, rounded up to SGD 5.55. That exceeds the 0.50 de minimis and is far below the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of 5.55.

Nothing else moves. There are no ERP, toll or surcharge lines to correct (0 gantry lines, no airport surcharge, so POL-RD-09 adds nothing and no billing-integrity referral arises). No driver compensation is due: the billed distance (27.3 km) is not less than the trace distance (27.28 km), so there is no unbilled-distance shortfall under POL-RD-04. The driver's profile does not establish a repeat-deviation pattern (deviation_flags_90d is 1; 1 ÷ 202 = 0.005), so there is no POL-RD-06 uplift and no driver-conduct referral. The profile fields mentioned in the claims — the rider's prior_disputes_filed and prior_disputes_upheld, and the driver's lifetime prior_deviation_flags — are context only under POL-GEN-01 and were not used as grounds of decision. The rider's deviation_claims_60d is 1, below the POL-RD-08 corroboration trigger, and the rider has discharged its initial burden in any event.

No escalation trigger fires: the trace is unimpaired (214 fixes, 10 s interval, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0), the trip identifiers match across trip record, trace and fare breakdown, timestamps are consistent, the refund is within limits, and no charge line is unmatched.
